newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Lots of launches.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Lots of launches.

text.p: Asian debt markets were busy on Tuesday with several new issues launches.
Tri Polyta Indonesia started the show by pricing its US$185 million Yankee bond overnight in New York.
The 11.375 percent seven-year senior secured notes were priced at 99.404 to yield 11.40 percent, or 540 basis points over the 5.875 percent Treasury note due 2004.
Other Indonesia deals also were in the news.
The Singapore branch of state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia set a three-year FRCD that pays an all-in of 52.5 basis points. Overseas Union Bank was the lead.
And bankers said the PT April's FRN issue has been increased.
A bunch of South Korean issues also were among the offerings.
Seoulbank launched a US$100 million three-year floating rate note issue via SBC Warburg. The notes pay a margin of 44.5 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
That gives an all-in of 49 basis points, quite a bit more than the 42 basis points paid on its issue launched last April, which was not well received.
More recently, Seoulbank launched a 10-year callable step-up FRN that paid a coupon of 80 basis points over LIBOR to the call in year five. Fees were 40 basis points.

Korea French Banking was in with a five-year, three-year put floating rate certificate of deposit issue that pays a coupon of 50 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in of 62 basis points. Fuji International Finance and Bank Berliner Group ran the books.
Industrial Bank of Korea set a US$110 million three-year FRN via lead manager BZW. The notes were launched at 99.875 to float at 10 basis points over LIBOR. Fees were 15 basis points.
South Korea's opposition parties today agreed to ratify the country's membership in the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, which the Paris-based club offered on October 11.
In other debt news, a couple of new Hong Kong dollar deals started syndication, while another deal closed.
Wing Hang set a HK$200 million two-tranche FRCD, while Rabobank's Hong Kong branch launched a HK$400 million two-tranche fixed rate CD off its new HK$1.5 billion CD programme.
And bankers said Bank of East Asia's FRCD was increased to HK$2.3 billion from HK$1.8 billion in syndication.
